name: rule-did-not-fire
prompt: fixture_rule_did_not_fire.py is our 24 V buck board. My 0.5 mm width on the VIN input rail isn't taking: the route between the two input caps comes out at 0.15 mm. Why? Fix it without losing the board defaults.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_rule_did_not_fire.py, Design RuleDidNotFireDesign; lc_power_board.py imports box from lc_radio_board.py. Every rule in the fixture sits at priority 0. The buck board (lc_power_board.py) removes the TPS62933 library circuit's own three rules (a 0.25 PowerNetTag width and 0.25 SwTag and BstTag clearances, all priority 0) and keeps its tags, so the design carries only the rules the fixture states. Measured on the bare fixture (this suite's own run, 2026-11-03): the VIN route came back at 0.15, the default IsTrace width. The skill's priority section says equal priority between matching rules is not defined; the fix is a distinct priority above every rule that matches VIN (1 or more), with the defaults kept. Measured on this suite's own solution: priority 1 gives 0.5, no issue. A runner that removes the default rule, or calls it fixed without reading the realized width, fails. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, in the fixture module, fixture_rule_did_not_fire.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A diagnosis that the 0.5 rule and the 0.15 IsTrace default both match the VIN trace at priority 0, where the order is not defined; the 0.5 rule raised to a priority above them; the defaults kept; and COMPLETION.md with the measured VIN width after the build.

assertions.text: the VIN route is realized at 0.5 mm on every trace shape, and the board's 0.15 default width rule is still in the design
the diagnosis names priority as the cause: the rail rule ties with the 0.15 IsTrace default, which also matches the VIN trace, and equal priority does not decide which wins
the fix gives the rail rule a distinct priority above every rule that matches the VIN trace, and does not delete or loosen the defaults
COMPLETION.md reports the VIN width read from the built design, not build success alone
